observations: Handheld electronic device with a pistol-grip handle and a color touchscreen.
The screen is powered on and displays 'Welcome', 'Printed: 0', and 'Remain: 100000'.
A white cardboard box is present with a line drawing of the device and 'CE' and 'RoHS' certification marks.
A small rectangular item, likely an ink cartridge, is visible inside a clear plastic wrapper.
No brand name or model number is visible on the device casing or the front of the box.
The device appears to be a generic handheld inkjet coder used for printing dates or logos.

claims.evidence: The physical form factor and the UI on the screen in photo 0 are characteristic of a handheld inkjet coder.
Suitability for branding depends on the print resolution and ink adhesion to specific materials, which cannot be tested remotely.

risks.proof: A video of the device successfully printing a line of text or a logo onto a piece of paper.
A photo of the underside of the device showing the print head or a photo of the specification sticker.
A video showing the device operating and printing while not connected to a charging cable.

proof_requests: Photo of the specification sticker, usually located on the back of the device or inside the battery compartment.
Video of the device performing a test print to verify the ink cartridge and print head are functional.
Photo of the underside of the device to see the size of the print head.
response.reason: The specific model and print height capacity are not visible. These specifications, along with proof of a functional print head, are required to distinguish between a low-value entry-level unit and a professional coder.
